correctness.rationale: C: For a cubic 14-vertex 21-edge graph, any deleted k-set gives c=2k−7−e(S) when its complement is a forest; hence k>=4 and any successful 4-set is independent with connected 10-vertex, 9-edge complement. The Fano 4+0, 3+1, and 2+2 split proof is exhaustive and establishes both sufficiency and impossibility. Seven lines and their duals yield 14 type A; seven lines times four off-line retained points and their duals yield 56 type B. The 168 collineations and side-swapping polarity give the 336 automorphisms and two orbit sizes. The packaged standard-library verifier enumerates all 16384 subsets, matches all 70 sets and both tree-degree signatures, and verifies 336 graph automorphisms and orbit actions. The finite computation corroborates, not replaces, the unrestricted combinatorial proof for this fixed graph.

value.rationale: V: The Heawood graph is the canonical cubic point-line incidence graph of the Fano plane; minimum feedback vertex sets exactly encode maximum induced forests/trees. The count of *all* minimum sets and structural dichotomy into two non-isomorphic complementary trees is a natural complete optimizer classification, with two automorphism orbits of orders 14 and 56. It distinguishes symmetry/robust solution diversity not captured by the easily known minimum size alone, and the exact incidence proof explains why no mixed 2+2 optimizers exist. This is a self-contained structural classification rather than a marginal bound or arbitrary parameter slice.
